title: Staleness/refresh process + data-currency badges + drift detection
context: Open datasets are updated periodically. Without a staleness process, published explainers silently show outdated figures without readers knowing it — eroding trust and potentially misleading decisions. Each explainer must record its data vintage and refresh cadence; drift in an upstream release should automatically open a maintenance refresh task. The shared toolkit must surface a data-currency badge on every explainer artifact.
objective: Define and document the staleness/refresh process, integrate data-currency badges into the shared toolkit, and specify a drift-detection approach that opens a refresh task when an upstream source updates.
acceptanceCriteria: Each explainer records a data vintage (source retrieval date and version) and a refresh cadence; drift in an upstream release automatically opens a maintenance refresh task.
Re-running the committed derivation code regenerates published figures from the pinned source snapshot (reproducibility verified end-to-end).
A data-currency badge showing the data vintage is included in every delivered explainer artifact.
The staleness/refresh policy is committed as a document (e.g. REFRESH.md) and the drift-detection approach is integrated into or documented alongside the shared toolkit (toolkit-002).
resources: TASKS.md — refresh-021 acceptance criteria and M3 exit criterion
toolkit-002 (prerequisite — shared toolkit must exist before drift detection can be integrated)
output: A committed staleness/refresh policy document (REFRESH.md or equivalent) + data-currency badge implementation + drift-detection approach integrated into or documented alongside the shared toolkit (toolkit-002).
